facts: **$V = \pi r^{2}h$**, where $r$ is the radius of the circular cross-section and $h$ is the perpendicular height (or length) of the cylinder.
This is just $V = Ah$ with $A = \pi r^{2}$, so a cylinder is handled exactly like a prism.
The formula uses the **radius**, so halve the diameter before substituting when a diameter is given.
$\pi r^{2}h$ means $\pi \times (r \times r) \times h$: square the radius first, then multiply by $\pi$ and by the height.
Leaving the answer as a multiple of $\pi$, such as $63\pi$ cm³, gives the **exact** volume.
A rounded decimal answer is written with $\approx$.
Use the calculator value of $\pi$, keep the working exact and round only at the last line, to the form the question asks for.
A radius and a height in centimetres give a volume in cm³.
steps: Substitute the radius, halving the diameter first if one is given, and the height.
Evaluate, then round or leave in terms of $\pi$ as asked.

workedExamples.question_text: A cylindrical rod has a circular cross-section area of $15\text{ cm}^{2}$ and a length of $8\text{ cm}$. Find its volume.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The length is the perpendicular distance between the circular ends.
$\begin{align*}V &= Ah\\&=15\times8\\&=120\text{ cm}^{3}\end{align*}$

The radius is $2\text{ cm}$ and the perpendicular height is the $13\text{ cm}$ length.
$\begin{align*}V &= \pi r^{2}h\\&=\pi\times2^{2}\times13\\&=52\pi\text{ cm}^{3}\\&\approx163.36\text{ cm}^{3}\end{align*}$

The radius is half the diameter.
$\begin{align*}r &= \frac{4}{2}=2\text{ m}\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}V &= \pi r^{2}h\\&=\pi\times2^{2}\times3\\&=12\pi\text{ m}^{3}\\&\approx37.7\text{ m}^{3}\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A cylindrical tin has an internal radius of $3\text{ cm}$ and an internal height of $10\text{ cm}$. It contains $200\text{ cm}^{3}$ of paint. Find the empty space inside the tin, correct to two decimal places.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}V_{\text{tin}} &= \pi r^{2}h\\&=\pi\times3^{2}\times10\\&=90\pi\text{ cm}^{3}\end{align*}$
Subtract the paint volume from the tin’s internal volume.
$\begin{align*}V_{\text{empty}} &=90\pi-200\\&\approx82.74\text{ cm}^{3}\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: Cylinder A has radius $3\text{ cm}$ and height $12\text{ cm}$. Cylinder B has diameter $8\text{ cm}$ and height $8\text{ cm}$. Find both volumes in exact form. State which is larger and find the difference, correct to two decimal places.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Cylinder A:
$\begin{align*}V_A &=\pi\times3^{2}\times12\\&=108\pi\text{ cm}^{3}\end{align*}$
Cylinder B has radius $8\div2=4\text{ cm}$.
$\begin{align*}V_B &=\pi\times4^{2}\times8\\&=128\pi\text{ cm}^{3}\end{align*}$
Cylinder B has the greater volume.
$\begin{align*}\text{Difference} &=128\pi-108\pi\\&=20\pi\text{ cm}^{3}\\&\approx62.83\text{ cm}^{3}\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A cylinder with radius $3\text{ cm}$ and height $6\text{ cm}$ fits exactly inside a cube with edge length $6\text{ cm}$. Express the cylinder’s volume as a percentage of the cube’s volume, correct to one decimal place.

A cylindrical container has internal radius $4\text{ cm}$ and internal height $10\text{ cm}$. It is full of water. The water is poured into an empty rectangular container with internal dimensions $10\text{ cm}$ by $8\text{ cm}$ by $7\text{ cm}$. Will all the water fit? Justify your answer using volumes correct to two decimal places.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}V_{\text{cylinder}} &=\pi\times4^{2}\times10\\&=160\pi\text{ cm}^{3}\\&\approx502.65\text{ cm}^{3}\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}V_{\text{box}} &=10\times8\times7\\&=560\text{ cm}^{3}\end{align*}$
All the water fits because $502.65\text{ cm}^{3}<560\text{ cm}^{3}$.

development.question_text: A cylindrical water tank has a diameter of $3$ m and a height of $2$ m. Find its volume in m³, correct to $1$ decimal place.

development.solution_text:
Cylinder A: $V = \pi \times 5^{2} \times 9$
$= 706.8583\ldots \approx 706.86\text{ cm}^{3}$
Cylinder B: $r = \frac{12}{2} = 6$
$V = \pi \times 6^{2} \times 6$
$= 678.5840\ldots \approx 678.58\text{ cm}^{3}$
$706.86 - 678.58 = 28.28$
Cylinder A is greater, by $28.28$ cm³.

mastery.question_text:
A cylinder of radius $4$ cm and height $8$ cm fits exactly inside a cube of edge length $8$ cm.
Express the volume of the cylinder as a percentage of the volume of the cube, correct to $1$ decimal place.

Cylinder A has a radius of $6$ cm and a height of $10$ cm.
Cylinder B has a radius of $12$ cm and a height of $5$ cm.
Find both volumes in exact form in terms of $\pi$, and state which cylinder has the greater volume.
mastery.solution_text:
Cylinder A: $V = \pi \times 6^{2} \times 10$
$= 360\pi\text{ cm}^{3}$
Cylinder B: $V = \pi \times 12^{2} \times 5$
$= 720\pi\text{ cm}^{3}$
Cylinder B has the greater volume, because $720\pi\text{ cm}^{3} > 360\pi\text{ cm}^{3}$.

mastery.question_text:
Marta fills a cylindrical container of radius $5$ cm and height $11$ cm with water.
She pours the water into an empty rectangular box measuring $12$ cm by $8$ cm by $9$ cm.
Using volumes correct to $2$ decimal places, decide whether all of the water fits, and justify your answer.
mastery.solution_text:
Cylinder: $V = \pi \times 5^{2} \times 11$
$= 863.9379\ldots \approx 863.94\text{ cm}^{3}$
Box: $V = 12 \times 8 \times 9$
$= 864\text{ cm}^{3}$
All of the water fits, because $863.94$ cm³ is less than the box’s $864$ cm³ — but only just, with about $0.06$ cm³ to spare.
